name: Banco do Brasil
focus: Agribusiness and rural-credit economics: client concentration, subsidized/equalized lines, repricing, collateral, restructurings and loss migration; distinguish policy mechanisms from unsupported assumptions about political intervention.
Public-sector relationships, payroll/retail, corporate and SME franchises; test how client/product mix changes margins and funding stability.
Credit recoveries, discounts and provisioning alongside NPL and coverage; distinguish a quarterly profit rebound from a credit-cycle inflection.
Treasury, insurance/affiliates, pension-related contributions and tax effects; reconcile their role in recurring and accounting results.
Capital generation/distribution and expected-loss transition: separate Resolution 4,720 legacy tables from CMN 4,966 presentation.
traps: Some spreadsheet cells are BRL displayed as millions; others are thousands or already millions.
Agribusiness is separately classified in selected credit tables; do not add it to PF/PJ figures that already include it.
Published narrative, current workbook and original quarter can use different expanded-credit definitions.

name: Bradesco
focus: Banking versus insurance/pensions/capitalization: isolate revenue, underwriting/claims, financial income, capital and profit contributions.
Transformation execution: distribution footprint, high-income/SME client propositions, digital engagement, technology costs and realized productivity.
Client versus market NII, liability margins, secured origination and SME collateral realization; test risk-adjusted returns rather than equating collateral with safety.
Provisions, Stage 3 migration, restructurings, recoveries and credit cost across the recovery cycle.
Recurring versus accounting profit, fiscal/labor adjustments, administrative expense reclassifications and capital distribution.
traps: The mapped historical ROE is YTD annualized; quarterly ROAE in releases is a different series.
Managerial and accounting balance sheets have different consolidation perimeters.
Insurance strength does not by itself establish improvement in the banking franchise; broader operating expenses are not a common peer denominator.

name: BTG Pactual
focus: Business-line economics: investment banking, corporate lending, sales/trading, asset management, wealth/personal banking, consumer finance and interest/other results.
Recurring management fees versus performance/transactional revenues, client flows versus market appreciation, and the quality of AuM/WuM monetization.
Pan and other acquisitions: compare original/perimeter-adjusted history, integration effects, goodwill and capital use; isolate organic growth.
Corporate and consumer credit quality separately, concentrations, guarantees, collateral and underwriting; do not infer low risk from an absent retail NPL metric.
Funding mix, maturity, secured/unsecured funding, market risk, RWA intensity, liquidity buffers and capital allocation between franchises.
traps: AuM/WuM are client assets, not bank assets or revenue; avoid unsupported double counting.
Balance-sheet loans differ from the corporate-plus-consumer business portfolio.
Reported operating expenses include items excluded from adjusted efficiency; reported expenses/revenue does not reproduce that ratio.
Call transcripts and thematic reviews are available under data/calls and the bank knowledge directory; consult latest_calls.json for exact coverage and outstanding gaps.

name: Caixa Econômica Federal
focus: Housing/mortgage concentration, duration, funding sources and policy-linked economics; distinguish the bank's balance sheet from funds it administers.
Savings, term deposits, credit letters and other funding: pricing, maturity and dependence on housing funding mechanisms.
Retail/commercial PF/PJ, infrastructure and agribusiness: contribution, loss concentration and portfolio weights; a small distressed book can have a high ratio without characterizing the whole bank.
Government services, payments, cards, insurance distribution and asset management as fee franchises; quantify scale, monetization and expense absorption.
Recurring versus accounting profit, provisions/write-off criteria, legal/actuarial items, capital requirements and distributions.
traps: ROE and efficiency in the key-figures tables are trailing 12 months.
Quarter, YTD and annual values coexist on the same PDF page; superscript footnotes can be mistaken for numbers.
Customer deposits, broad funding and administered assets have different scopes; FGTS administered assets are not automatically bank funding.
Call transcripts and thematic reviews are available under data/calls and the bank knowledge directory; consult latest_calls.json for exact coverage and outstanding gaps.

name: Itaú Unibanco
focus: Brazil versus LATAM results, client/product mix, FX, credit volumes and asset/liability margin contributions.
Retail/high-income, SME/corporate, wealth/investments, insurance, payments/cards and investment banking: contribution and cross-sell economics, not client counts alone.
Pricing discipline, credit quality by segment, Stage 2/3, write-offs and recoveries; assess returns alongside RWA/capital and cost of risk.
Digital/distribution productivity, recurring fee growth, expense seasonality and changes in service economics.
Acquisitions including Avenue, managerial reclassifications, goodwill/tax adjustments, OCI and capital return; isolate perimeter effects.
traps: Consolidated ROE and Brazil-only ROE differ; do not choose whichever makes a ranking look stronger.
Pro forma historical series and original 2024 reporting are not interchangeable.
The funding aggregate includes securities/borrowings and is not simply customer deposits.
The historical workbook is a supplemental official-page link; verify its current replacement for a new release.

name: Santander Brasil
focus: Client-margin changes through mass-market selectivity, consumer financing, SME/corporate, product spreads and liability mix; test deliberate risk reduction versus lost competitiveness.
Funding composition, PF/PJ mix, customer primacy, pricing and maturity; connect to margin and liquidity outcomes.
Wholesale-specific provisions, retail/consumer vintages, restructurings and revised write-off criteria; reconcile NPL movements with provisioning and Stage 3.
Cards, insurance, consortia, brokerage and other fees versus lending dependence; measure profitability and distribution strength where disclosed.
Managerial/accounting reconciliation, goodwill exclusions, exceptional provisions, expense discipline, taxes and capital return.
traps: ROAE excludes goodwill; the accounting-profit base differs from recurring managerial profit.
Legacy 2024 sheets use thousands where current tables use millions.
Stage 3 coverage is not NPL90 coverage; certain historical ratios exclude extraordinary provisions.
A falling NPL ratio alongside rising provisions needs migration/write-off/denominator analysis, not an automatic improvement verdict.
